# 佛說大乘造像功德經

**ID:** T0694
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 唐 提雲般若譯
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 692
**Juans:** 2
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0694

## Contributors
- 提雲般若 (A001210)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T694 in two fascicles is the most extensive of the early Chinese Buddhist sūtras on the Udayana sandalwood-Buddha-image tradition, translated by the Khotanese translator [Devaprajñā](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E9%9B%B2%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) (active in Cháng'ān / Luòyáng under Empress [武則天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AD%A6%E5%89%87%E5%A4%A9) Wǔ Zétiān) at the imperial translation programme. The colophon "大唐于闐三藏提雲般若奉制譯" ("translated by imperial decree by the Tripiṭaka Devaprajñā of Khotan, Great Tang") attributes the rendering to imperial commission, dated by the *Kāiyuán shìjiào lù* 開元釋教錄 ([KR6s0093](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0093), T2154) to the period 689–691 CE.

**Abstract**

The setting is unique among the Udayana-image sūtras: the Buddha preaches the sūtra in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three (Trāyastriṃśa, 三十三天) under the Pāriśātaka tree (波利質多羅樹), with Maitreya as the principal interlocutor — locating the discourse precisely at the moment in the Buddha's biography when King Udayana (back on earth) was commissioning the first Buddha-image. The structural innovation is to make the *zàoxiàng* (image-making) doctrine the substantive content of what the Buddha was preaching to his mother and the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa during the same period — thus uniting the legend's two ends (the Buddha in heaven; Udayana on earth making the image of the absent Buddha) into a single doctrinal narrative.

The work is a substantial expansion of the brief older versions [KR6i0382](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0382) / T692 and [KR6i0383](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0383) / T693; it incorporates the doctrinal apparatus of late-seventh-century Chinese Mahāyāna Buddhism (the bodhisattva path, the merit of image-making in relation to the *pāramitās*, the cosmic-buddha visualization), and treats the Udayana legend as the canonical scriptural ground for the entire Mahāyāna Buddhist image-cult. The text was widely cited in Tang and Sòng liturgical and apologetic literature.

Related canonical texts: earlier short versions [KR6i0382](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0382) (T692), [KR6i0383](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0383) (T693); related cluster on image / stūpa merit [KR6i0385](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0385)–[KR6i0390](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0390).
